samples.summary: New `failFromBackend` login error envelope has no test on any of its three call sites
samples.evidence: `login.ts` replaces three prose `console.error(...)+process.exit(1)` failure paths (token exchange, `/auth/me`, `/workspaces`) with `failFromBackend`, which parses the backend body and emits `backendErrorEnvelope(...)`. The only login test (`packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts`) mocks every backend call to return `jsonResponse(...)` with status 200, so no test ever drives a non-ok response through `failFromBackend`. Grepping `packages/cli/test` for `failFromBackend`, `Token exchange failed`, `Failed to fetch user info` returns nothing. Untested consequences include whether the envelope is actually emitted once, whether the message survives, and whether execution really stops (the call sites `await` a helper typed `Promise<never>` while the code after continues to `exchangeRes.json()`).

samples.summary: The `sawUnboundCode` timeout diagnostic is new behavior with no coverage
samples.evidence: The callback server now tracks `sawUnboundCode` when a callback arrives with `state === null` and swaps the timeout message for a server-predates-the-echo hint. `login-callback.test.ts` does fetch `/callback?code=evil-1` with no state (asserting 400), but never triggers the timeout path, so nothing asserts the flag changes the rejection message. No test in packages/cli greps for the substring 'carried no `state`'.

samples.summary: `command: commandPath(this)` threading into the import/upload/download orchestrators is untested end-to-end
samples.evidence: Five actions now pass `command: commandPath(this)` into `runDocsImport`, `runNotesImport`, `runSlidesImport`, `runFilesUpload`, `runFilesDownload`. The orchestrator suites (`docs-import.test.ts:307`, `notes-import.test.ts:232`, `slides-import.test.ts:359`, `files-upload.test.ts:123-223`, `files-download.test.ts:139`) call the `run*` functions directly and never pass or assert `command`; the only `command`-bearing assertions are on the builders (`output.test.ts:227-233`) and on `outputError` paths. So dropping `command:` from any one of those five wiring sites would leave the whole suite green.

samples.summary: Negative guard assertions use optional chaining, so they also hold when no state was stored at all
samples.evidence: `stateFor` returns `undefined` when the guard stored no state token, and the rejection tests assert `expect(stateFor({...})?.nonce).toBeUndefined()` (nonce over-bound, empty nonce, array nonce, `code_challenge: 'short'`, malformed challenge). Because `undefined?.nonce` is `undefined`, these pass whether the guard correctly stored a state with no nonce or wrongly stored nothing at all — they do not distinguish 'value rejected' from 'whole CLI flow broken'. Asserting the state object exists (e.g. `expect(state).toMatchObject({ mode: 'cli' })`) before checking the field would make them discriminating.

samples.summary: No test that a CLI login without a nonce still produces a redirect with no `state` param
samples.evidence: The controller builds `stateEcho` conditionally (`state.nonce ? '&state=…' : ''`). The nonce-present case is covered by 'echoes the CLI nonce back as `state`' (auth.controller.spec.ts:218), but the no-nonce branch is only touched by the pre-existing test at line 190, whose assertion is `stringMatching(/^http:\/\/127\.0\.0\.1:9876\/callback\?code=.+/)` — that regex matches equally if a stray `&state=undefined` were appended, so the backward-compat shape is unasserted.

samples.summary: New `codeVerifier` DTO constraint (@IsOptional/@IsString/@Length(43,128)) has no validation test
samples.evidence: All exchange tests call `controller.cliExchange({...})` directly, bypassing the global `ValidationPipe` in `main.ts`; one of them even passes `codeVerifier: 'nope'` (4 chars), which a real request would reject at the pipe with 400 rather than reaching the store. Other DTOs in this repo do have pipe-level tests (`datasource.dto.spec.ts:36`, `miro.controller.spec.ts:433`), so the pattern exists but was not applied here — nothing catches a decorator being dropped, or the 43-char lower bound colliding with the CLI's exactly-43-char `randomBytes(32).toString('base64url')` verifier.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: login.ts's three new failure paths (lines 82-87, 99-104, 118-123) route through failFromBackend (lines 173-181), which emits backendErrorEnvelope and exits. The only test importing src/commands/login.js is test/login-callback.test.ts, whose fetch stub returns jsonResponse(...) hardcoded to status 200 (lines 65-70, 111-132), so no non-ok response ever reaches failFromBackend; its assertions concern the OAuth URL nonce/mode and the PKCE verifier hash only. Candidate counterexamples fail: output.test.ts:225-336 unit-tests the backendErrorEnvelope builder in isolation, output.test.ts:563-584 drives a non-ok response through `docs content` (not login), and ctx.test.ts:110-119 covers a missing session in `ctx`. Repo-wide greps for failFromBackend, the three fallback message strings, auth/cli/exchange, commands/login, and registerLoginCommand surface no other test; vitest.config.ts:5 limits the suite to test/**/*.test.ts and no *.test.ts exists under src, so there is no alternate test root. The backend spec (auth.controller.spec.ts:313) tests the server endpoint, not CLI rendering. Result: envelope-once, message preservation, and flow termination at the login call sites are untested — a changed behavior with no meaningful test, major under the test-adequacy rubric.

mergedFrom.summary: New nonce ingestion in GitHubAuthGuard has no test at all

finding.summary: New nonce plumbing in `GitHubAuthGuard` (query capture + 1..128 length bound) has no test at all
finding.evidence: The guard now reads `req.query.nonce` and stores it only when `typeof nonce === 'string' && length > 0 && length <= MAX_NONCE_LENGTH` (github-auth.guard.ts:26-38). There is no `github-auth.guard.spec.ts` — `ls packages/backend/src/auth/*.spec.ts` yields auth.controller, cli-auth.store, auth.service, jwt.strategy, github.strategy only — and a repo-wide grep for `GitHubAuthGuard` in tests returns nothing. The controller spec exercises the echo by calling `cliAuthStore.createState('cli', 9876, 'n0nce-x/y')` directly (auth.controller.spec.ts:220), bypassing the guard entirely. So the middle link of the chain (browser query → stored state) is untested: dropping the nonce read, inverting the length check, or accepting an array-valued `?nonce=` would keep every suite green.

verdict.reason: A dedicated spec for the guard exists at packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.spec.ts and covers precisely the cases the finding names as untested. (1) Nonce read from query to stored state: spec:51-58 invokes the real guard.canActivate with {mode:'cli',port:'9876',nonce:'n0nce-x/y'} and reads it back through a real CliAuthStore (store.consumeState(req.__cliStateToken), spec:44-49), so removing the req.query?.nonce read at github-auth.guard.ts:59 breaks it. (2) Length bound: spec:60-70 asserts 128 chars is kept and 129 is dropped, so inverting the bound check at github-auth.guard.ts:26 breaks it. (3) Array-valued ?nonce=: spec:76-79 explicitly asserts nonce ['a','b'] yields undefined, covering the typeof value !== 'string' guard at github-auth.guard.ts:25. Not over-mocked: only the inherited Passport mixin canActivate is stubbed (spec:29-37); the guard's own logic, boundedToken, and CliAuthStore are all real. The file is collected by the unit suite via testRegex ".*\.spec\.ts$" (packages/backend/package.json:106), so it is not orphaned. The finding's claim that listing packages/backend/src/auth/*.spec.ts yields only five specs is contradicted by the working tree; my own glob and a grep for "nonce" both return this file. The controller spec bypassing the guard is irrelevant because the guard has its own direct coverage.

finding.summary: No test asserts the CLI actually sends `&nonce=` on the OAuth start URL it later gates on
finding.evidence: login.ts:42-46 mints the nonce and appends `&nonce=<enc>` to the OAuth URL; the callback server then rejects any callback that does not echo it (login.ts:206). The only new CLI test, test/login-callback.test.ts, calls `startCallbackServer('the-nonce')` in isolation and never drives `registerLoginCommand`'s action. If the `&nonce=` param were dropped or misnamed, the backend would echo no `state`, the CLI would 400 its own genuine callback and hang until the 30s timeout — and both the new CLI test and the backend controller test (which seeds the nonce into the store directly) would still pass.

verdict.reason: The finding's factual premise is false in this working tree. packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts contains a second describe block ('wafflebase login', lines 87-163) that registers the real command (registerLoginCommand at line 101) and drives its action via program.parseAsync(['login']) at line 134. It captures the actually-printed OAuth URL from console.error, then asserts the `nonce` query parameter specifically: oauthUrl.searchParams.get('nonce') at line 140 with expect(nonce).toBeTruthy() at line 143 — exactly the assertion the finding says is absent. If `&nonce=` (login.ts:55) were dropped or misnamed, get('nonce') would be null and that assertion fails; additionally the test feeds the extracted nonce back as `state` to the real listener (lines 147-150) and asserts 200, so a wrong param name would also fail the nonce gate at login.ts:241 and the flow would never reach the exchange assertions at lines 154-162. The test is not over-mocked on the point at issue: the fetch spy passes loopback requests through to realFetch (line 114), so the real callback server and nonce comparison run; WAFFLEBASE_SESSION (line 97) is honored by src/config/session.ts:38-39 so the action completes to saveSession and `await done` resolves. One meaningful test covering the claimed-missing behavior is enough to refute an absence claim.

finding.summary: Nonce-mismatch coverage only exercises the length-differs branch, so a length-only comparison would pass
finding.evidence: `nonceMatches` (login.ts:164-169) is `a.length === b.length && timingSafeEqual(a, b)`. The test's two rejection cases are no state at all and `state=guessed` (7 chars) against `the-nonce` (9 chars) — both short-circuit on the length check, so `timingSafeEqual` is never reached with a mismatching same-length value. Replacing the body with `return a.length === b.length` (accepting any 9-char attacker state) leaves the suite green. A same-length wrong-value case (e.g. `state=xxx-nonce`) is what would pin the actual comparison.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the nonce-mismatch coverage only exercises the length-differs branch, but the cited test file contains a third rejection case that is exactly the same-length wrong-value case. `startCallbackServer('the-nonce')` (login-callback.test.ts:22-23) is probed with `state=xxx-nonce` (login-callback.test.ts:38-41) — 9 bytes, identical in length to `the-nonce` — so `a.length === b.length` at login.ts:198 is true and `timingSafeEqual` must return false for the asserted 400 (login.ts:241-245) to occur. Replacing the body with `return a.length === b.length` would make that request return 200 and fail `expect(sameLength.status).toBe(400)`. The suite also pins the accept path (`state=the-nonce` -> 200, `waitForCallback()` resolves 'real', lines 45-50), so an always-false implementation fails too. The finding's stated evidence ("the test's two rejection cases are no state at all and state=guessed") is contradicted by the file, which has three rejection cases including the one it says is missing.
